chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the wicked (immoral) woman, can the man marry her? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If there is a slave girl for him, he can copulate with her, but he should not take her as a mother of his children'.

key_terms.أُمَّ الْوَلَد: Mother of the child; a female slave who bears her master's child and gains specific legal status.
key_terms.الْخَبِيثَة: The immoral or wicked woman, often referring to one known for fornication or specific vices.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying an immoral woman versus taking her as a concubine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while a man may marry an immoral woman (al-khabithah), he should not elevate her to the status of 'umm walad' (mother of the child) if he already possesses a slave girl, preferring instead to have relations with the slave girl. This ruling highlights the juristic distinction between the legal status of marriage and concubage, emphasizing the preservation of the slave girl's rights and status in the household hierarchy. The hadith reflects the practical application of marital laws in early Shia jurisprudence, where the choice between a free wife and a concubine carried specific legal implications for inheritance and lineage.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the wicked (immoral) woman, can the man marry her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there is a slave girl for him, he can copulate with her, but he should not take her as a mother of his children’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man if he could marry the filthy (prostitute). He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If he has a slave-girl with whom he has gone to bed but she must not be taken as the mother of his children.’” (He must use contraceptives)
